trust_decision.summary: The dashboard decides, in getRedirectURL alone, that the OAuth2 redirect_uri origin may be the raw request Host whenever the operator-declared DashboardHost is empty; the published commit for this advisory rewrites only that function's doc comment to declare the empty value an intentional configuration boundary, so no behaviour is closed.

landing_point.why: getRedirectURL is the only constructor of the OAuth2 callback URL; the advisory names dashboard_host and redirect_uri, and this 12-line function is where the Host header is either pinned or trusted.

fix_sites.module_kind: http_controller, comment-only doc change (no behavioural change in the published commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The settings merge route is an admin-only PATCH (cmd/dashboard/controller/controller.go:191 + adminHandler at :257-272), while the advisory's attacker is an unauthenticated request with a forged Host, so a solver can call the settings form a separate configuration concern instead of part of the redirect_uri fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Dynamic / multi-domain deployments are documented as legitimate: a Host listed in ReservedHosts must stay trusted, and DashboardHost may deliberately differ from InstallHost (agent connect host). Pinning every redirect to InstallHost, or refusing any non-DashboardHost host, breaks both; the pinned tree has tests asserting exactly these two behaviours.

O6_input_shapes: raw Host as sent by the client (arbitrary attacker value)
DNS absolute name with trailing dot (panel.example.com.)
comma-separated ReservedHosts entries with spaces and empty items
X-Forwarded-Proto: https on a plain request
published diff handles none of these: it adds no code (fix.diff:13-19)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second absolute-URL builder that takes scheme+Host from the request and embeds a bearer transfer token, with no operator allowlist.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists next to the OAuth flow and a maintainer writing a new public URL (MCP base URL, install command, webhook target) would copy this pattern, since nothing in the codebase forces URL origins through IsReservedDashboardHost.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-provider callback override that builds the redirect_uri from a provider-specific host instead of the shared guard (e.g. a second provider setup path).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same value is re-fed into Oauth2Config.Setup at oauth2.go:226 from cached state, so a maintainer adding a bind/provider-specific flow could plausibly construct a URL there from the request instead of the cached one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second host allowlist (websocket/origin checks) that trusts the request Host without the same normalisation as IsReservedDashboardHost.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cmd/dashboard/controller/mcp_origin.go:27,38 already compares c.Request.Host for origin checks, so a maintainer adding a redirect or CORS allowlist would naturally write a second, slightly different comparison.

O9_family: CWE-601 URL redirection to untrusted site via Host header injection into the OAuth2 redirect_uri

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.5 (go.mod:3), modules only, no vendor dir; cgo sqlite (mattn/go-sqlite3, go.mod:25); package main needs placeholder cmd/dashboard/{user,admin}-dist dirs and swag-generated docs to build (//go:embed *-dist at cmd/dashboard/main.go:40, CI at .github/workflows/test.yml:37-48)
O10_build.project_tests: cmd/dashboard/controller/oauth2_test.go:115-195 unit-tests getRedirectURL with gin/httptest and in-memory sqlite (oauth2_test.go:35), no network; full suite is `go test -mod=readonly -count=1 ./...` (.github/workflows/test.yml:44-45). Affected packages build and test without the frontend dist, which is absent from the checkout.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Fall back to Conf.InstallHost when DashboardHost is empty and pin everything to it, which breaks the documented dashboard_host/install_host decoupling asserted by oauth2_test.go:145-153.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit bundles an unrelated hardening (privileged Service.Type allowlist reaching model/service.go, cmd/dashboard/rpc/service_dispatch.go, service/singleton/servicesentinel.go, controller/service.go) for a different advisory; it is not part of this OAuth2 advisory and was not screened.

cmd/dashboard/controller/mcp_transfer.go:351-356 builds an absolute URL from the raw request Host (and X-Forwarded-Proto) with a bearer transfer token and no operator allowlist; noted only, not pursued, because it is not the OAuth2 redirect_uri sink.
unverified: The published source change for THIS advisory is comment-only (fix.diff:5-22 rewrites the getRedirectURL doc comment); it documents the empty-DashboardHost passthrough as intentional and points at GHSA-rf68-8gjr-36q7. No code behaviour is closed, so Pattern A ('published scope') cannot be derived from the diff and any hidden test would have to come from the advisory text, not the fix.

O2 (setting.go:101-103) is a judgement call: updateConfig unconditionally overwrites DashboardHost/ReservedHosts from a string-typed form with no omitempty-preserve (model/setting_api.go:10-12) and saves via applyEnableMCPTransition, so any partial admin PATCH clears the pin. It only becomes a security-relevant site if the fix chooses a fallback rather than failing closed; a fail-closed guard at oauth2.go:37-41 plus an error return at oauth2.go:66-67 is a single-file fix, so treat single_site risk as high despite the flag not being set by definition.
The settings step is not persisted in an obvious reload path beyond Conf.Save writing config.yaml; I did not verify a restart round-trip (no execution allowed).
